2608.05028.title: Language Models Generalize to Human-like Word Order Preferences
2608.05028.paper_summary: A central question in language acquisition is whether linguistic biases can emerge from general learning mechanisms operating over underdetermined input. Artificial Language Learning (ALL) studies have shown that human learners reliably generalize beyond the evidence provided, including by preferring scope-homomorphic noun phrase modifier orders. In this work, we investigate whether language models exhibit the same bias under similar conditions. We create a controlled learning environment in which models are trained on a corpus where all noun phrases containing multiple modifiers have been removed, eliminating direct evidence about modifier ordering, and are then evaluated on multiple modifier sentences. Across three model sizes, we find that they consistently prefer scope-homomorphic orders despite never observing them during training. These preferences vary in strength by modifier type. To investigate the source of these preferences, we examine noun-modifier association strength using pointwise mutual information (PMI). While PMI reflects known modifier-ordering patterns, it does not explain the models' ordering preferences. These findings demonstrate that LMs can recover human-like linguistic generalizations from impoverished input and provide a controlled framework for investigating the mechanisms underlying such biases.
2608.05028.paper_summary_zh: 一個關於語言獲得的核心問題是，語言偏見是否可以從在不確定輸入上運作的一般學習機制中產生。人工語言學習（ALL）研究顯示，人類學習者可靠地超越所提供的證據進行概括，包括偏好範疇同構的名詞短語修飾語順序。在這項工作中，我們調查語言模型在類似條件下是否表現出相同的偏見。我們創建了一個受控的學習環境，在這個環境中，模型在一個去除了所有包含多個修飾語的名詞短語的語料庫上進行訓練，消除了有關修飾語排序的直接證據，然後在多個修飾語句子上進行評估。在三種模型大小中，我們發現它們始終偏好範疇同構的順序，儘管在訓練期間從未觀察到這些順序。這些偏好根據修飾語類型的不同而有所變化。為了調查這些偏好的來源，我們使用點對點互信息（PMI）檢查名詞-修飾語的關聯強度。雖然PMI反映了已知的修飾語排序模式，但並未解釋模型的排序偏好。這些發現表明，語言模型可以從貧乏的輸入中恢復類似人類的語言概括，並提供了一個受控的框架來調查這些偏見背後的機制。
2608.05028.author: Amanda Popadich et.al.
